messages:
Maria G: quick follow-up on the ingress RFC — I dug into client disconnect semantics and we need to decide how the edge treats partial streams vs retries. Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4123 :eyes:

Josh K: quick note: current gateway retries are blind for streaming routes. that causes duplicate payloads for backends that have side effects.

Rachel S: agree. Two obvious approaches: 1) require idempotency keys for any retryable streaming request, 2) make retries off by default for streaming and only enable per-route.

Anand P: tradeoff: forcing idempotency makes client work harder (not all SDKs will send keys), but safe. per-route opt-in is safer for compatibility but increases config surface and could lead to silent failures when users expect retries.

Levi T: another idea — don't retry at transport level for streams. instead implement resume tokens and allow backends to support resume from offset. proxy can surface resume token header on disconnect so SDKs can reconnect and continue. less risky than transparent retry.

Maria G: resume tokens are appealing. implementation note: we'd need a small KV store for short lived resume tokens and mapping to backend cursor. That pushes state into edge tho.

Josh K: true. stateful edge increases operational complexity. alternative: have the backend return a short-lived resume token and the proxy just passes it through (stateless proxy). backend stores cursor. proxy still needs to forward on reconnect routes.

Rachel S: that keeps edge simple. sample headers we discussed in RFC:

```
X-RW-Resume-Token: <opaque-token>
X-RW-Idempotency-Key: <client-generated-id>
X-RW-Retry-Policy: none|idempotent-only|always
```

Maria G: +1 for those headers. we should also clarify abort vs client disconnect: do we abort backend work immediately on disconnect or keep running for short tail (5s) to allow reconnect?

Anand P: recommended heuristic: wait 3s for reconnect, then mark request as aborted. keep-ahead window configurable per route. This balances cost and UX.

Levi T: note on metrics: we need to tag requests that were aborted due to client disconnect vs real failure so SLO math is correct. add a label like gateway.disconnect_reason = reconnect_timeout|client_abort|backend_error.

Rachel S: ops concern: if we add resume tokens and per-route retry flags we need a migration plan for existing routes. propose default behavior for existing routes: streaming retries OFF, resume token OFF, idempotency optional. Then roll opt-ins for critical customers.

Maria G: full plan:
- Phase 1: document headers, disable transparent streaming retries globally, add metrics for disconnects and aborted streams.
- Phase 2: support backend-provided resume token (stateless proxy). SDKs learn to use token and reconnect flows.
- Phase 3: optional proxy-managed resume (stateful) for high-value clients behind dedicated capacity.

Josh K: opsec question: resume tokens must be short lived and signed by backend to avoid abuse. recommend HMAC with expiry embedded.

Anand P: agree. also rate-limit reconnect attempts per token to prevent hot loops.

deploy-bot: staging gateway rolling deploy succeeded for commit 7a3f2d8 — streaming retries disabled by default (flags: streaming_retries=false).

Maria G: thanks — can someone add a short RFC follow-up PR with the phased rollout and sample headers? I can draft the text for phase 1.

Rachel S: i'll open the PR and tag @anand @josh.

Josh K: I'll add metric instrumentation and a dashboard widget for disconnect_reason counts. :thumbsup:

Levi T: I'll write a tiny SDK example for using resume token (JS + python snippets) once the headers are finalized.

Maria G: great, sounds like consensus. closing thread for action items.
